case.background: Two like point charges repel in vacuum. Sphere radii are negligible relative to every listed separation; charges remain fixed, and polarization, image forces, and external fields are absent. Determine how the force magnitude depends on the two charges and their separation.
initial_observations: The deflection is reproducible and reverses direction when the sphere positions are exchanged.

controls.description: Magnitude of charge on sphere one.
controls.name: charge_1_nc

controls.description: Magnitude of charge on sphere two.
controls.name: charge_2_nc

instruments.description: A vacuum torsion balance with two effectively point-like charged spheres, independently calibrated charges, and adjustable center-to-center separation.
instruments.name: electrostatic_torsion_balance

notes: This is a deterministic idealized benchmark world, not a literal replay of a historical data table.
A valid experiment changes only listed controls and consumes one episode attempt.
The historical branch uses the vacuum point-charge idealization.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'electrostatic_power_law'. FinalSubmission.parameters must contain exactly reference_force_un, charge_1_exponent, charge_2_exponent, distance_exponent. Candidate law: F = reference_force_un*(charge_1_nc/5)^charge_1_exponent*(charge_2_nc/5)^charge_2_exponent*(separation_cm/10)^distance_exponent
